column1: CX - Implement improve for phone-number validation
column32:
The current phone-number validation query only returns the first matching row. However, the same phone number can appear in more than one field or record, so stopping at the first match can leave valid matches unevaluated. This can cause the backend to continue with the wrong phone number context and return incorrect feedback or responses to the user.

Improve the validation logic so the query is handled correctly by creditor and/or every matching result is evaluated before deciding which phone number should be used for validation and user feedback.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* The validation logic does not stop after the first matching row when the same phone number appears in multiple fields or records.
* All matching query results are evaluated to determine the correct phone number context before returning a validation response.
* The query or filtering logic correctly considers the creditor so the backend selects the phone number associated with the intended creditor.
* User-facing feedback and backend responses are based on the correct validated phone number and do not return incorrect results caused by evaluating the wrong match.

column1: CP - BACK - Auth - Lockout bypass, account enumeration and missing attempt limits in password reset, identity check and shared-email login
column32:
h2. Description

Found while adding unit test coverage in [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1930|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1930|smart-link]. Some auth flows let someone guess a password or SSN digits without a limit, and some reveal whether an account exists. The only protection they have today is the shared per-IP Ingress limit.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Reset confirm doesn't reveal whether a password is correct without a valid code.
* Reset verify and confirm are rate-limited per email (same as HED-1935) and give the same response for unknown and existing emails.
* The identity check stops after a limited number of attempts.
* Shared-email login is rate-limited per email (same as HED-1935). Wrong passwords still don't count toward any account's lockout, and a locked account matched by its correct password still returns "locked out", as decided in HED-1938.
* Onboarding steps are rejected unless a token was issued and hasn't expired.
* Normal reset, login and onboarding work as today.



h2. Initial Findings

* *Reset confirm checks the password before the code.* {{password/reset/confirm}} is anonymous and has no per-email limit. It returns {{password_same_as_current}} before validating the code, so a password can be guessed with only an email, and the attempts don't count toward the lockout.
* *Reset verify/confirm reveal accounts.* An unknown email returns {{no_user_data_found}}; an existing one returns {{otp_wrong_reset}}.
* *The identity check has no attempt limit.* SSN-last-4 and date of birth can be retried without limit in the same onboarding session.
* Onboarding steps are rejected unless a token was issued and hasn't expired.
* Normal reset, login and onboarding work as today.

column32:
h2. Description

Found while adding unit test coverage in [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1930?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNGVjOGRmZjk5YzYzNGRmNjg3YjdiZDBhM2QwYTdhNzYiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1930?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNGVjOGRmZjk5YzYzNGRmNjg3YjdiZDBhM2QwYTdhNzYiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link]. Several auth flows can be used to guess passwords or SSN digits without triggering the lockout, or reveal whether an account exists. Their only protection today is the shared per-IP Ingress limit.

h2. Initial Findings

* *Reset confirm checks the password before the code.* {{password/reset/confirm}} is anonymous, has no per-email limit, and returns {{password_same_as_current}} before validating the code. A password can be guessed with only an email, without counting toward the lockout.
* *Reset verify/confirm reveal accounts.* Unknown emails return {{no_user_data_found}}; existing ones return {{otp_wrong_reset}}.
* *The identity check has no attempt limit.* SSN-last-4 and date of birth can be retried without limit in the same onboarding session.
* *Shared-email login skips the lockout.* When an email matches several Forth clients, wrong passwords don't count as failed attempts, and a locked account still confirms a correct password.
* *The onboarding token check accepts an empty token* (defense in depth). Today a request without a token is rejected earlier by model validation.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Reset confirm doesn't reveal whether a password is correct without a valid code.
* Reset verify and confirm are rate-limited per email (same as HED-1935) and respond the same for unknown and existing emails.
* The identity check stops after a limited number of attempts.
* Failed shared-email logins count toward the lockout, and locked accounts give the same response for any password.
* Onboarding steps are rejected without an issued, non-expired token.
* Normal reset, login and onboarding work as today.

column1: CP - BACK - Add Unit Test Coverage for Authentication Service
column32:
h2. Description

The authentication service changed significantly in a short period: 

* Account resolution against Forth ([https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1594|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1594|smart-link])
* The first-login entry point and onboarding step reorder ([https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1595|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1595|smart-link])
* Duplicate-email login handling ([https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1938|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1938|smart-link])
* Per-email rate limiting on onboarding start and password reset ([https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1935|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1935|smart-link])
* The production lock on the testing reset endpoint ([https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-2044|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-2044|smart-link]). 

All of it was validated manually, with Postman and in the browser, and none of it has automated tests.

The testing spike created by [~accountid:712020:bba04ff1-46ba-4373-b0a0-5581ead637b3] ([https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1636|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1636|smart-link]) deferred auth testing because login code was stable, and set the condition to re-evaluate it "when substantial authentication changes are scheduled". 

That condition is met now. This ticket adds unit tests for the decision logic of the authentication service, covering at minimum every scenario implemented and manually tested in those tickets.

It follows the setup and conventions established by [~accountid:712020:bba04ff1-46ba-4373-b0a0-5581ead637b3] in [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1677|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1677|smart-link] for Creditors ([https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1795|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1795|smart-link], [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1796|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1796|smart-link]).

Tests are grouped by flow and named after the scenario they cover, so the catalog below also serves as the source for the flow documentation in [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1854|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1854|smart-link].

References:

* [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/x/BYBHIw|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/x/BYBHIw|smart-link] 
* [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/x/BQBHIw|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/x/BQBHIw|smart-link] 
* [HED-1795|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1795]: Unit tests for the debt domain rules on Creditors (PR [#180|https://github.com/cordoba-tech/cordoba-consumer-portal-backend/pull/180])
* [HED-1796|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1796]: Unit tests for the creditors handlers (PR [#182|https://github.com/cordoba-tech/cordoba-consumer-portal-backend/pull/182])

h2. *Acceptance Criteria*

* -An auth test project follows the conventions from [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1795|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1795|smart-link], is part of the solution, and runs in the PR check.-
* -Every scenario in the catalog has at least one passing test.-
* -Tests are grouped by flow and named after the scenario, so the catalog can be read directly from the test names.-
* -Tests cover the service's decision logic with Identity's responses substituted. Identity's own behavior stays as deferred integration testing, per the spike.-
* -No test reaches Forth, Redis or the database.-
* -No production behavior changes. The only production changes are the ones needed for testability, listed under Approach.-

h2. Approach

* *One production change, for testability only:* {{CustomersRepository}} now depends on {{IForthRestApiClient}} instead of the concrete {{ForthRestApiClient}}. DI already resolves both to the same singleton, so behavior is unchanged. Verified with a full local onboarding and login.
* {{userManager.Users}} async queries run against a small in-test helper ({{Support/AsyncQueryable}}) instead of adding MockQueryable or EF InMemory. The spike advises against InMemory, and the helper adds no new dependencies.

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
h2. Findings (ticketed separately)

Writing these tests surfaced production issues outside this ticket's scope. They're grouped in the epic [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-2101|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-2101|smart-link]:

* HED-2103: lockout bypass and account enumeration in password reset, no attempt limit on the identity check, and no per-email guess limit on shared-email login.
* HED-2104: onboarding can be completed without accepting Terms or setting a password
* HED-2099: login lockout not cleared after a password reset; reset can leave the account without a password
* HED-2105: unreadable Forth contact ids handled inconsistently
* HED-1610: SPIKE, session handling across backend, web and mobile
* HED-2008: iOS password rules don't match the backend (backlog)
{panel}

h2. Deliverables

PR: [https://github.com/cordoba-tech/cordoba-consumer-portal-backend/pull/216|https://github.com/cordoba-tech/cordoba-consumer-portal-backend/pull/216|smart-link] 

h2. Scenario catalog

Grouped by flow. Each group lists the test class where its scenarios can be read from the test names.

*Forth lookup*: {{CustomersRepositoryTests}} (HED-1594, HED-1938)

* No match, or only co-applicants → not found.
* One match → found, with the contact mapped from Forth. A client sharing the email with their own co-applicant still counts as one match.
* Two or more matches → every candidate is reported and none is picked. An unreadable id doesn't turn a duplicate into a single match.
* The contact can't be loaded from Forth → not found.
* Forth errors reach the caller instead of being reported as "not found".

*Login*: {{UserSignInServiceLoginTests}} (HED-1594, HED-1595, HED-1938)

* Email not in Forth, Forth email different from the one typed, or no local account → invalid credentials.
* The account is found by Forth contact id, not by email.
* Onboarding not finished → invalid credentials, without checking the password.
* Account locked → locked out with the remaining minutes, without checking the password.
* Empty password → password required.
* Correct password: with 2FA required, the code is sent with its target masked and the account is synced from Forth; without 2FA, tokens are issued.
* Wrong password → counted toward the lockout and no sync. The attempt that crosses the limit → locked out.
* The sync would collide with another account → duplicate account login blocked.

*Login with an email shared by several Forth clients*: {{UserSignInServiceLoginTests}}

* Empty password → password required.
* Only the account whose password matches signs in, synced from its own Forth contact. Accounts of other clients are never tried.
* No password matches → invalid credentials. The password matches more than one account → duplicate account login blocked.
* For the matched account:
** email conflict on sync → blocked;
** contact can't be loaded, or its Forth email changed → invalid credentials;
** onboarding not finished → invalid credentials.
* Wrong passwords don't count toward any account's lockout. A locked account matched by its correct password → locked out with the remaining minutes (HED-1938 decision).

*Login code, refresh and logout*: {{UserSignInServiceSessionTests}}

* Code for an unknown user → invalid credentials. Account locked → locked out, without checking the code.
* Wrong code → counted toward the lockout. The attempt that crosses the limit → locked out. Expired code → OTP expired.
* Valid code → session for the device, code used up, failed attempts reset, "remember this device" passed on, device linked for notifications.
* Refresh → same session, with the refresh token rotated. A token that belongs to another user, is unknown, revoked or expired → rejected.
* Logout → session closed and device unlinked.

*Onboarding start*: {{UserOnboardingServiceStartTests}} (HED-1594, HED-1595)

* Email shared by two Forth clients → multiple customers found, no account created.
* Email not in Forth → customer not found. A local account still holding that email is resynced from its own Forth contact.
* New client → account created and code sent.
* Existing unfinished account, found by contact id even if the email changed → synced and reused, no duplicate account.
* Account already onboarded → synced, then already onboarded.
* Email held by another account → email already registered. If resyncing that account frees the email → the client continues.

*Onboarding steps*: {{UserOnboardingServiceStepsTests}}, {{OnboardingAccessTokenServiceTests}} (HED-1594, HED-1595)

* Code confirmation:
** unknown user, already onboarded, wrong code or expired code → the matching error and no token;
** valid code → token issued and email confirmed.
* Access token: issued with the configured lifetime, replaces any earlier one, and is rejected if different or expired. Without a valid token, or once onboarding is finished, every step is rejected and nothing is saved.
* Agreement: both documents required. Acceptance dates and the version of each document in the client's language are recorded, and onboarding is not marked completed.
* Password: invalid → validation errors; valid → password set.
* Identity: wrong SSN or date of birth → identity mismatch. Verified → onboarding completed. The device is linked only when a push token is sent.

*Forth sync*: {{UserForthSyncServiceTests}} (HED-1594, HED-1938)

* Same email (case-insensitive) → profile updated, email untouched.
* New email free locally → email and username updated.
* New email held by another account → email conflict. Email and username kept; the rest of the profile still synced.
* Identity rejects the email or username → original values restored.

*Password reset and change*: {{UserPasswordServiceTests}}, {{PasswordCharacterRulesValidatorTests}}

* Reset request: unknown email or wrong SSN digits → the same generic error, no code sent. Match → code sent.
* Reset code check: doesn't use up the code. Wrong and expired codes get different errors.
* Reset confirm:
** wrong or expired code → password unchanged;
** password breaks the rules → errors, code kept;
** valid → password replaced and code used up.
* Change while signed in: wrong current password, same password, or rules broken → rejected before any SMS. With 2FA required, the password changes only after the SMS code is confirmed.
* Password rules: one of {{!@#$%^&*}} is required, and spaces are not allowed. Both errors are reported at once.

*Per-email rate limit*: {{EmailRequestRateLimiterTests}} (HED-1935)

* Onboarding start and password reset check the limit (3 attempts in 15 minutes) before doing anything.
* Over the limit → 429 with {{auth.email_rate_limit}} and the remaining minutes, rounded up.
* The email is normalized and hashed in the key, and each action has its own counter.
* Redis unavailable → request refused (fail-closed).

*Testing reset endpoint*: {{ResetOnboardingEndpointTests}} (HED-2044)

* In production → 404, and the reset never runs. Local, development and stage were verified manually in HED-2044, since a test process can only run under one environment.

column1: CP - BACK - SPIKE - Review session handling across backend, web and mobile
column32:
*Description:* 

Found while adding unit test coverage in HED-1930. Several issues point to session handling as a whole, not to isolated bugs. We need a complete picture of how sessions, refresh tokens and device ids work across backend, web, iOS and Android before deciding what to change.

*Initial Findings:*

* Login removes an existing session by device id only, not by user, so one client can end another client's session on the same device id.
* Refresh tokens are stored in plain text.
* Refresh tokens are rotated, but a reused old token doesn't revoke the session, and every refresh extends the expiry by 7 days.
* The web only sends a device id after "remember me". Otherwise the backend generates a new one on every request, so web sessions are never cleaned up.
* Changing or resetting the password doesn't end other sessions.

column32:
h2. Description

CreditorX Android and iOS customers are currently seeing a generic *“Error”* message when attempting to log in with valid credentials. This message does not explain the root cause or provide enough information to reproduce or diagnose the problem.

Previous research by [~accountid:712020:f5e366c6-65b6-45ab-af69-01a539ce9b27] indicates that the generic error appears when the Kazoo login flow fails. The issue only occurs when the customer’s login credentials are valid. When credentials are invalid, the client correctly returns the message *“User not found or incorrect”*.

Additional investigation is needed to identify why Kazoo fails during valid login attempts, improve observability around the failure, and return a clearer error message to the customer when this scenario occurs.

[~accountid:712020:f5e366c6-65b6-45ab-af69-01a539ce9b27] also noted that, during each login attempt, the system changes the password in Kazoo because the Kazoo user password is required to authenticate against the Kazoo API. Since Kazoo does not provide an endpoint to retrieve the current password, the system creates a new password during each login attempt to know the active password.

!!!!But saying it's because of Kazoo is just a guess; with this error message, it's impossible to determine if Kazoo is the cause. Part of this task is figuring out what's causing the login to fail.

Moving this to Blocked.

While investigating this ticket I traced the call flow end-to-end: {{KazooController::handle()}} ({{app/Http/Controllers/Kazoo/KazooController.php}}) is invoked by Kazoo via {{POST /kazoo/number/handle}}, and it decides {{is_caller_known}} based on {{block_collectors}} and the creditor/blocked-phone tables. On the Kazoo side, the callflow this app provisions per account ({{KazooAPIClient::createCallFlow}}, see the {{is_lawyer_required}} module in {{app/Integrations/KazooAPIClient.php}}) matches a live custom Erlang module I found on the telephony server ({{cf_is_lawyer_required.beam}} on {{logic1}}). I decompiled it and confirmed it only reads a custom channel variable ({{Is-Creditor}}) to decide the branch — it does not call our backend directly.

I need to find where that {{Is-Creditor}} variable actually gets set (i.e., whatever component makes the real HTTP call to {{/kazoo/number/handle}}), since that's outside this repo. 03/Nov/26 10:58 PM;712020:dac1dce4-8aa1-4b7e-8cd4-12205fb8c6e4;*CaseTrack ↔ Forth note sync: investigation and fixes*

*Reported problem:* Notes weren't syncing in either direction between CaseTrack and Forth for the test client (*For testing*: Forth contact 871536280, CaseTrack client 29297).

*What we found*

* *The app and infrastructure are healthy.* Over the last 30 days, production pushed about 2,900 notes to Forth and processed about 31,000 note updates from Forth. The server, the message queues, and the Forth API login all worked, and no code or deployment issue was involved.
* *CaseTrack → Forth already worked.* A client-level test note showed up on the Forth contact within seconds. Notes sent from a case or debt go to that debt's notes in Forth, not the contact's Notes tab. Forth also displays times two hours behind CaseTrack. Both made synced notes easy to miss.
* *Forth → CaseTrack had three configuration problems in Forth:*
*# The production note trigger ("CT Create notes", 68697) excluded the test company, so the test client's notes never reached production. They only went to the dev and staging webhooks, which were failing.
*# No production trigger existed for debt notes. Debt notes added in Forth never reached CaseTrack, for any client.
*# The "RSC-PROD Task update" webhook pointed at the dev server instead of production.

*Changes made*

* Removed the test-company exclusion from trigger 68697. It now fires for every Legal note.
* Created the production webhook "RSC-PROD Pull Debt notes" (36620) and the trigger "CT Pull debt notes" (83076), so debt notes now sync to production.
* The "RSC-PROD Task update" webhook was repointed to production.

*Remaining notes and recommendations*

* Only Legal-type contact notes sync from Forth. This is by design, but worth confirming.
* Notes from any *test-company* contact now reach production.
* Code improvements to consider:
** Log failed and successful pushes to Forth.
** Handle Forth's intermittent 401 errors, which currently crash the retry logic about 6,600 times a month.
